messages.content: You are a bounded research analyst. Return a concise prose memorandum, not JSON. Distinguish facts in the supplied prior art from your recommendations. Do not invent repository capabilities, current production facts, authority, revenue, or newsroom outcomes.

We need the smallest executable next step that turns Koios.News from one-story-at-a-time scheduling into a Rendanheyi publication portfolio without weakening its journalism. Use only this packet.

PRIOR ART — IETF-conformant clickbait: The central object is an attributed, time-indexed claim with provenance and editorial status, not the article. Attention surfaces may intensify curiosity but never certainty. Demand may create assignments but not evidence. Every surface should project from a richer editorial state; corrections propagate to article, headline, social card, feed, schema, and archive. Business value is generating and monetizing many attention surfaces without losing claim accountability. Slogan: make the click, preserve the warrant, propagate the correction.

PRIOR ART — accountable attention: Optimize informed satisfaction rather than raw CTR. Surfaces must preserve entailment, source relation, uncertainty, scope, proportionality, payoff sufficiency, image integrity, commercial transparency, and correction readiness. Service journalism can legitimately use urgency when it states the deadline, eligibility, proof needed, and payoff. Generate headline variants only after claim extraction; reject allegation-to-fact, correlation-to-causation, possibility-to-certainty, local-to-general, and preprint-to-proof strengthening.

PRIOR ART — agentic newsroom: Demand-to-assignment separation, genre contracts, authority graphs, source-power/source-diversity measures, omission records, legal/harm gates, and correction dependency invalidation are required. Editorial judgment is not reducible to one score. Reader demand creates reporting questions, not answers.

PRIOR ART — recommender-game equilibrium: Metrics become production commands. Search/ad systems reward volume, freshness, keyword match and monetizable traffic, creating farms and mills. Raw clicks can reward manipulation; accuracy, usefulness, originality, satisfaction, and civic value do not collapse into one metric. A sustainable design must measure them separately and prevent one proxy from swallowing the production objective.

RECOVERED EXECUTABLE PRIOR ART: content-mill carriers already exist for privacy-preserving article performance by path/section/tag and ad performance by provider/path/day/section/tag, including impressions, clicks, revenueMicros, RPM and CPC. Existing desk carriers represent beat, section, editorial frame, sources, wire freshness and article count.

CURRENT KOIOS STATE: The market-facing Koios ME buys an internal publication-cycle service from its Publication Operations node. Clockkeeper only transports the order. Current planning ranks candidates across service-utility, entertainment-celebrity, politics-power, business-consumer, technology-science, culture, environment, sports and investigations using source depth, recent scarcity, duplication, trends and observed loads. It currently chooses the first candidate that clears sourcing, then runs one expensive writer/editor circuit. Four daily issue opportunities exist, but this is not yet a true mixed portfolio, has no explicit cross-subsidy allocation, and has no product-specific inference/cost envelope. Attention and revenue are recorded but sparse; revenue is still zero and may not be invented. Writers have source-depth gates and editorial assessment.

Rendanheyi constraint: Koios owns the reader relation and value pool. Internal node microenterprises sell it sourcing, writing, editorial, surface, publication and learning services. Internal transfers are not external value. Node participation is settled only against externally evidenced reader/revenue value after attributable costs.

Deliver a prose memo with exactly these headings: Recovered Mechanism; First Executable Portfolio Move; Why This Precedes More Desks; Acceptance Evidence. Recommend one bounded implementation that reuses the carriers and existing planner. It must define a portfolio/slate object, allocation rules across cheap attention products and expensive depth products, product-specific source/editorial/cost floors, and exact evidence proving it improved behavior. Keep it under 1,500 words.

completion.text:
**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Koios Engineering and Editorial Leads
**FROM:** Research Analysis
**SUBJECT:** Transition to Rendanheyi Portfolio Management

### Recovered Mechanism
The current Koios operation treats the publication cycle as a serial process: rank candidates, select one, execute. To move toward a Rendanheyi structure—where internal nodes (microenterprises) compete for internal budget by providing services to the reader-relation pool—we must shift the planning unit from the "Article" to the "Portfolio Slate." 

Existing "Desk Carriers" (beat, section, editorial frame) already categorize content, while "Content-mill Carriers" track performance metrics (RPM, CPC, impressions). The mechanism for a portfolio shift lies in re-tasking the current planner to output a *Slate Object*—a pre-set mix of high-velocity (attention-capture) and high-depth (accountable-journalism) products—rather than a single selection. This allows the Publication Operations node to treat the four daily issue slots as a cross-subsidized portfolio rather than a sequence of independent gambles.

### First Executable Portfolio Move
Implement a "Slate Allocation Rule" within the existing planner. Instead of choosing the single best candidate, the planner must now select a balanced slate of four daily items based on the following heuristic: one "Service" product (high utility/low cost), two "Beat" products (medium cost/high accountability), and one "Investigation" product (high cost/high authority). 

This move uses the existing Desk Carriers to apply specific "Product Floors." 
*   **Service Floor:** Requires low source-depth, high-utility focus, and strict adherence to urgency protocols (deadline/proof/payoff). 
*   **Depth Floor:** Requires high source-diversity scores and verified editorial gates. 

By enforcing a cost/risk envelope for each slot, the Publication Operations node creates a market where "Service" products act as the attention-anchor, funding the "Investigation" products. This ensures that the journalism budget is protected by the portfolio’s aggregate performance rather than the success of a single item.

### Why This Precedes More Desks
Expanding the number of desks prematurely would fragment the attention pool and increase coordination overhead without introducing market discipline. The current bottleneck is not a lack of editorial desks but a lack of internal accounting for how content serves the broader publication goals. Establishing the Slate Allocation Rule first creates the "Internal Transfer" price signals necessary for Rendanheyi. Once the nodes (Sourcing, Writing, Editorial) are required to bid against a portfolio envelope, Koios can accurately measure which beats are self-sustaining and which require cross-subsidy, providing a data-driven justification for adding or cutting specialized desks later.

### Acceptance Evidence
Acceptance of this model will be evidenced by the decoupling of "Attention Metrics" from "Journalism Quality." Success is reached when:
1.  **Portfolio Variance:** The slate achieves stable traffic across the four slots despite varying depth levels, proving the "Service" products are effectively insulating the "Investigation" products from market volatility.
2.  **Attributable Costs:** The internal cost of production for each item is mapped against its reader-relation contribution (measured through the existing Content-mill Carriers). 
3.  **Correction Readiness:** The preservation of "Correction Readiness" (as per Prior Art) is confirmed by the automated propagation of corrections across the entire Slate Object. 

If the Investigation products maintain their source-depth gates while the Service products maintain their utility-metrics without cannibalizing the editorial authority of the brand, the portfolio move is successful. Accuracy, usefulness, and civic value must be measured independently of CTR to ensure the recommender-game equilibrium remains aligned with the editorial mission.
